title: Domain, Range, and Graph of the Least Integer Ceiling of Sine
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Graph y = \sin x and the least integer function y = \lceil \sin x \rceil together. Determine the domain and range of \lceil \sin x \rceil.

steps.title: Determine the Natural Domain
steps.explanation: Since sin x is defined for all real x and the ceiling function is defined for all real inputs, the domain of ceiling(sin x) is (-infinity, infinity).
steps.why: Composing two functions whose domains are all real numbers yields a function defined on (-infinity, infinity).

steps.title: Partition the Values of sin x in [-1, 1]
steps.explanation: At the troughs x = 3*pi/2 + 2k*pi where sin x = -1, ceiling(sin x) = -1; on (-1, 0], ceiling(sin x) = 0; and on (0, 1], ceiling(sin x) = 1.
steps.why: By definition, ceiling(u) is the smallest integer greater than or equal to u.

steps.title: State the Range
steps.explanation: Collecting the three possible integer outputs gives the range {-1, 0, 1}.
steps.why: The only integers that are ceilings of numbers in [-1, 1] are -1, 0, and 1.
